target: Fault geometry absent from the supplied USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue, not geothermal vents or generic prospectivity. All local scores are visible-catalogue proxies; hidden-label performance is unavailable.

prior_art_method.scope: 582 public documents across 54 owner repositories; documents were keyword-selected, not a complete code/branch/literature audit.
prior_art_method.novelty_rule: No hypothesis below is called a globally untried family. Differences describe the exact operator relative to this repository and the inspected sibling documents; term hits establish documented prior art, not implementation or performance.
prior_art_method.gemsdoe53_check: The GEMSDOE53 default branch has one 11-byte README containing only '# GEMSDOE53'; GitHub API reports no other branch or file. No substantive H53 method was available to compare.

common_validation.stage2: 3x3 contiguous spatial blocks with a 12-pixel (1.2 km) training buffer; six truth-bearing blocks retained by the fixed plan; 250,000 negative samples, seed=fold index; 2.4-pixel NMS; emissions and DTI scoring restricted to the held-out block; M/|G|=3.47.
common_validation.comparator: incumbent H-D (58 physical features plus four scarp-facing-coherence features), evaluated on the same blocks and random seed.
common_validation.promotion_rule: A candidate must beat H-D on the locked aggregate and show a defensible paired-fold pattern. AUC is secondary. No weekly/competition slot is spent until that gate passes.
common_validation.caveat: Visible catalogue proxy holdouts can rank familiar fault styles only; they do not measure discovery of the hidden expert labels.

ranked_hypotheses.name: High-angle crossings of independent magnetic and gravity boundaries
ranked_hypotheses.status: IMPLEMENTED; matched six-block H-D add-on holdout complete; not promoted.
ranked_hypotheses.signature_operator: Normalized-convolution gradients at sigma=4 and 8 pixels (400 m, 800 m). At each scale, score axial discordance 1-|dot(g_TMI,g_gravity)|/(|g_TMI||g_gravity|), weighted by both edge magnitudes after robust scaling; suppress negligible edges. The score is a structural proxy, not a mapped fault.
ranked_hypotheses.geological_rationale: Great Basin geothermal systems commonly occur in fault intersections, terminations and transfer structures where permeability can be enhanced. Independent magnetic and gravity boundaries crossing at a high angle may flag a structure intersection that is not expressed as a single continuous surface scarp.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_prior_work: This repository's incumbent H-D uses LiDAR scarp-facing coherence; H-E uses co-located basement/conductivity/gravity derivatives. The new operator is high-angle, edge-weighted TMI–gravity discordance at two scales. It is NOT a new family: GEMSDOE26 H26-XEDGE and GEMSDOE27 H28-1 document gradient-orientation agreement; GEMSDOE49 documents magnetic–gravity orientation work. H53 contributed no substantive method.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_benefit_before_test: Low-to-moderate and uncertain; independent geophysical boundaries may identify intersections, but regional structures are not necessarily faults or geothermal conduits. No numeric uplift was preregistered; this was an exploratory screen.
ranked_hypotheses.implementation_cost: Low–medium: two existing rasters, two static derived channels, about 9 minutes for the six-fold baseline-arm run on this sandbox; matched-incumbent run costs another several minutes.
ranked_hypotheses.external_data: None; uses the mirrored competition geophysical rasters.

baseline_arm_result.comparability_note: This first H-G run replaced H-D's four coherence features with two intersection features (60 vs 62 total columns), so it is an informative arm comparison but not a matched addition test. Do not promote from it; the matched H-G + H-D run is required and is tracked separately.

ranked_hypotheses.promotion_status: NOT PROMOTED: matched mean proxy DTI delta -0.000606262 versus H-D (3/6 folds higher); no competition slot authorized.

matched_incumbent_result.comparability_note: Matched six-fold comparison: same fold IDs, held-out truth counts, block sizes, 250,000-negative seed plan, M/|G|=3.47, NMS/exclusion settings, and incumbent H-D feature set; H-G adds two TMI–gravity crossing channels. Mean proxy DTI is lower, with 3/6 folds higher; AUC is also lower. No promotion.

full_raster_experimental_artifact.decision: NOT SLOT-ELIGIBLE because the matched H-G+H-D holdout is below H-D.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Potential-field edge terminations with a conductive relay bridge
ranked_hypotheses.status: PROPOSED; not implemented or tested. Now the next proposal after the completed, negative H-G test.
target_layers: lidar step_max/coh100 as an independent surface check
ranked_hypotheses.signature_operator: Extract finite edge segments and endpoints from potential-field and basement-depth gradient ridges; identify spatially offset, approximately aligned terminations separated by 0.3–2 km, with a conductivity anomaly in the intervening bridge. Score only connected, multi-layer-consistent pairs; do not reward a generic edge-crossing or a single high-gradient pixel.
ranked_hypotheses.geological_rationale: Buried fault strands can terminate or transfer displacement beneath basin fill. Relay/transfer zones can host dense fracture networks; a conductive bridge between independently imaged structural terminations could be consistent with fractured or altered material. Conductivity is non-unique (clay, basin fill and lithology are alternatives), so this is a testable proxy, not proof of permeability.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_prior_work: H-E in this repository scores local co-location of basement, conductivity and gravity derivatives; H-G scores local high-angle edge crossings. H-H would represent finite edge endpoints and an offset bridge, i.e. segment topology rather than local co-location. Sibling work already explores relays/stepovers, fault tips and geophysical edge agreement (including GEMSDOE32 H33-5); therefore only this exact joint endpoint/bridge operator is a candidate variant, not an untried family.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_benefit: Qualitative, pre-test expectation: potentially moderate localization benefit over single-edge/co-location scores if paired terminations and a conductive relay bridge selectively mark fault-transfer corridors. No numeric DTI uplift is claimed; endpoint pairing and conductivity non-uniqueness make the sign uncertain.
ranked_hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium–high: edge thinning, graph construction, endpoint pairing, scale/offset controls and leakage-safe blocked ablation.
ranked_hypotheses.external_data: None; all candidate bands are present. USGS 2019 play-fairway reporting describes coincident/terminating gravity and magnetic gradients, low resistivity, temperature and structural settings as evidence in blind-system assessments; it does not validate this raster operator.
ranked_hypotheses.promotion_status: NEXT RESEARCH CANDIDATE, not promotion-authorized: preregister exact operator and controls, implement the matched spatial-block ablation, and require a pass against H-D before considering any slot.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Directional conductivity cross-edge contrast at blind basin margins
ranked_hypotheses.signature_operator: For independently detected basement/gravity/magnetic edge axes, measure robust conductivity contrast parallel to the axis versus across it at 150–800 m offsets and two smoothing scales. Rank an elongated along-edge conductor with a cross-edge basement/potential-field step above a broad isotropic conductive basin background.
ranked_hypotheses.geological_rationale: Fault damage zones and hydrothermal alteration can change electrical properties, while gravity/magnetic/basement contrasts locate structural boundaries. A directionally constrained conductor adjoining an independently observed boundary is more consistent with a fault corridor than conductivity magnitude alone, though clay-rich fill and lithologic contacts remain major confounders.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_prior_work: H-E already tested broad co-location of the three basin-edge layers and did not improve its matched holdout. This proposal tests anisotropy/offset of the conductivity response across a structural edge, not raw conductivity, edge magnitude or simple coincidence. The broader conductivity–structure and geophysical cross-gradient families have substantial sibling prior art; exact operator novelty is inspection-bounded only.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_benefit: Qualitative, pre-test expectation: low-to-moderate localization gain if an elongated conductivity response is directionally aligned with an independently observed basement/potential-field edge. Clay-rich fill and lithologic contacts may erase or reverse the signal; no numeric uplift is claimed.
ranked_hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium: masked directional filters, careful multiscale normalization, then matched blocked holdout; no new raster acquisition.
ranked_hypotheses.promotion_status: LOWER PRIORITY than H-H; do not implement until H-H receives a costed, preregistered screen or is rejected.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Earthquake-density modulation of independent structural edges
ranked_hypotheses.status: PROPOSED; semantics check required before implementation.
ranked_hypotheses.signature_operator: Conditional edge ranking: retain potential-field/basement edge segments only when they coincide with a local earthquake-density ridge and are not merely high everywhere in the broad seismicity field; compare against an edge-only model and a seismicity-only control on identical spatial folds.
ranked_hypotheses.geological_rationale: Recent earthquakes can indicate active structures not yet represented in a surface-fault inventory, while geophysical edges constrain where a subsurface boundary lies. The intersection could narrow a broad seismicity signal to a mappable fault corridor.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_prior_work: The supplied stack includes earthquake-distance/intensity products as ordinary features, and the sibling audit finds broad seismicity-lineament work. This candidate is the specific conditional interaction with an independently derived edge, not a claim that seismicity or lineaments are new.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_benefit: Qualitative, pre-test expectation: modest gain only if local seismicity concentrates on a structural edge; diffuse seismicity or catalog completeness gradients can create false associations. No numeric uplift is claimed, and viability is blocked pending source-band semantics.
ranked_hypotheses.implementation_cost: Low–medium after band definitions are authenticated; otherwise blocked.
ranked_hypotheses.external_data: No new acquisition proposed. The local competition band descriptions call these earthquake distance/intensity products, but the precise N=100 km/A=15° operator semantics should be checked against official band metadata before use.
ranked_hypotheses.promotion_status: NOT YET VIABLE; first verify source metadata and spatial support, then compare the interaction against matched edge-only and seismicity-only controls.

post_test_decision: The strongest low-cost hypothesis H-G's matched add-on test is complete. H-G added to H-D averaged 0.281056398 proxy DTI versus H-D 0.281662660, paired delta -0.000606262, and was higher in 3/6 folds. Its mean AUC was also lower (0.66962 vs 0.67262). It is not promoted and no competition slot is authorized. H-H–H-J remain lower-priority proposals; do not spend a slot unless a future candidate beats the locked H-D comparator.
